accessExperiment.scenario: Seven-card opening, first player, existing draw-focused Rai/Tonoris policies. Turns are checkpoints, not expected game lengths. Material presence is separate and does not imply playability.
accessExperiment.features: Context + quantities; then natural main-card access at each checkpoint, material presence, and policy coverage; then additional per-card access from paired shuffled-library simulations. Joint fit, not win rate multiplied by probability.
limitations: Unsupported draw engines are not modeled zero; both access models include policy indicators.
Extra access is a 128-sample estimate capped by remaining analytic unseen mass.
Current catalog/policies applied retrospectively; no actual in-game draw telemetry.
Repeated retrospective holdout; no prospective validation.

method.target: Match point share: win 1, draw 0.5, loss 0. One observation per match.
method.split: Frozen cutoff and end date from earlier composition experiment; current cached cohort within these dates. Retrospective holdout, not untouched future data.
method.baseline: Prior-day Elo frozen at cutoff; context adds signed champion within format and champion matchup within format. Format is recorded event format, not set/ban era.
method.cardAverage: Training-only per-card match-point rate with 20 neutral prior appearances, averaged by copies; prediction 0.5 + own average - opponent average. Both sides contribute to training counts.
method.adjusted: See accessExperiment: jointly fitted context, quantities, natural access, and optional extra draw access.
method.selection: Fixed turns 1/3/5 and 128 samples; feature vocabulary and coefficients training-only. No holdout tuning.
method.uncertainty: 400 paired event-cluster bootstrap samples; positive error reduction favors candidate. Does not account for cross-event player dependence.
limitations: No historical catalog or ban-era reconstruction
Exact unseen-deck subset does not isolate near-duplicate families
No causal interpretation of card coefficients
No prospective validation or larger groups
